title: Bowling Lane with Pin Collision Physics
prompt:
Create a single-HTML-file Three.js application simulating a bowling lane with a rolling ball, pin collisions, and score tracking.

【Three.js Import (must follow exactly)】
Place in <head>:
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>
Then in <script type="module">:
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';

【Scene Setup】
- Background: dark interior (#1a1a1a)
- Camera: perspective, starting at (0, 5, 12) looking at (0, 1, -8)
- Lights: spot light above the lane (warm white, casts shadows), ambient fill light, colored accent lights along the lane gutters (blue/purple)
- OrbitControls with damping

【Bowling Lane】
- Lane surface: long box (width 2.0, length 20, height 0.1), textured with hardwood2_diffuse.jpg (repeat along length)
- Lane extends from z=8 (near camera, player end) to z=-12 (pin end)
- Gutters: two channels on each side of the lane (width 0.3, below lane surface), dark material
- Foul line: a thin red line at z=5
- Approach area: z=5 to z=8 (slightly different shade)
- Pin deck area: z=-10 to z=-12 (slightly raised, 0.02m)
- Back wall at z=-13 to catch fallen pins

【Bowling Pins (10 pins in triangle formation)】
Arranged in standard triangle at the pin deck:
- Row 1 (front): pin at (0, 0, -10)
- Row 2: pins at (-0.3, 0, -10.52), (+0.3, 0, -10.52)
- Row 3: pins at (-0.6, 0, -11.04), (0, 0, -11.04), (+0.6, 0, -11.04)
- Row 4 (back): pins at (-0.9, 0, -11.56), (-0.3, 0, -11.56), (+0.3, 0, -11.56), (+0.9, 0, -11.56)

Pin spacing: 0.3m center-to-center horizontally, 0.52m between rows.

Each pin is modeled as:
- Geometry: a tapered cylinder (CylinderGeometry with radiusTop=0.04, radiusBottom=0.06, height=0.38) -- simplified bowling pin shape
- White material with red stripe bands
- Each pin is a rigid body with: position (x, y, z), velocity (vx, vy, vz), rotation, angular velocity
- Mass: 1.5 kg, moment of inertia approximated as solid cylinder
- A pin is 'standing' if its y-position is > 0.1 and angular tilt from vertical is < 45 degrees
- A pin is 'toppled' otherwise

【Bowling Ball】
- Sphere geometry, radius 0.11m (standard ball radius)
- Dark swirled material (use procedural noise or solid dark color with finger holes)
- Mass: 6.0 kg
- Ball starts at (aimX, 0.11, 7) -- aimX controlled by slider

【Ball Physics: Roll and Curve】
Ball rolling mechanics:
- Initial velocity: launched in -z direction with speed controlled by power slider (range 5-15 m/s)
- Spin: the ball has angular velocity around the vertical (y) axis, controlled by spin slider
- Hook/curve: spin creates a lateral force F_hook = spinCoeff * omega_y * v_z
  where spinCoeff = 0.3, omega_y is vertical spin, v_z is forward velocity
- This makes the ball curve left or right as it travels down the lane
- Lane friction: deceleration = 0.5 m/s^2 (ball slows as it rolls)
- Ball drops into gutter if |x| > 1.0 (ball x exceeds lane boundary)
- In gutter: ball rolls forward but cannot hit pins

【Collision Physics: Ball-Pin and Pin-Pin】
Ball-Pin collision:
- Sphere-cylinder collision detection (simplified to sphere-sphere with pin radius = 0.06)
- On collision: apply impulse-based collision response
  - Relative velocity at contact point
  - Impulse magnitude: j = -(1+e) * v_rel_dot_n / (1/m_ball + 1/m_pin)
  - Restitution e = 0.3
  - Apply impulse to both ball and pin
  - Pin gets knocked back and sideways, with angular impulse causing toppling

Pin-Pin collision:
- Check all pin pairs each frame for overlap (distance < pin_diameter)
- Apply same impulse-based collision response
- This creates the cascade effect where one pin knocks over others
- Pin-pin restitution e = 0.4

Pin toppling:
- Apply gravity torque: if pin tilts past center of mass, gravity accelerates the topple
- Simplified: if tilt angle > 15 degrees, add angular acceleration toward fallen state
- Pins rest on the deck: floor collision at y=0, pins cannot go below floor

【Game Flow】
1. AIM phase: player adjusts aim position and spin using sliders
2. Press 'Space' to LAUNCH: ball rolls down the lane
3. Ball reaches pins, collisions resolve
4. SCORE phase: after ball passes pins (z < -13) or 3 seconds after first pin contact, count standing pins
5. Knocked pins = 10 - standing pins
6. Press 'R' to RESET: clear pins, reset ball to start for next throw
7. Press 'N' for NEW GAME: reset all scores

Standard bowling scoring (simplified to single-frame):
- Display pins knocked per throw
- Track cumulative pins knocked across throws
- Strike detection: all 10 pins in one throw

【Controls】
(1) Aim position slider (id='slider-aim'): range -0.8 to 0.8, step 0.05, default 0 (ball x-position at launch)
(2) Power slider (id='slider-power'): range 5 to 15, step 0.5, default 10 (launch speed in m/s)
(3) Spin slider (id='slider-spin'): range -5 to 5, step 0.5, default 0 (vertical angular velocity, positive = curves right)
(4) Keyboard: 'Space' to launch, 'R' to reset frame, 'N' for new game, 'C' to toggle camera angle (overhead vs side)

【HUD (id='hud')】
Semi-transparent panel at top-left:
- id='hud-score': Total pins knocked
- id='hud-standing': Pins currently standing (0-10)
- id='hud-ball-speed': Current ball speed (1 decimal)
- id='hud-ball-pos': Ball z-position (1 decimal)
- id='hud-spin': Applied spin value
- id='hud-phase': Current game phase (AIM / ROLLING / SCORING)

【State Management】
Update window.__3D_STATE__ every frame:
{
  frameCount: number,
  score: number,                // cumulative pins knocked
  pinsStanding: number,         // currently standing (0-10)
  pinsKnocked: number,          // knocked this throw
  ballPos: {x, y, z},          // ball world position
  ballSpeed: number,            // ball scalar speed
  ballSpin: number,             // current spin value
  aimX: number,                 // aim slider value
  launchPower: number,          // power slider value
  phase: string,                // 'aim' | 'rolling' | 'scoring'
  isStrike: boolean,            // true if all 10 knocked in one throw
  pinStates: [boolean],         // array of 10 booleans, true=standing
  isPaused: boolean,
  simTime: number
}

【Physics Constraints】
- Ball must curve based on spin (left spin curves left, right spin curves right)
- Pin cascade: hitting front pin at center should topple most/all pins (strike)
- Pin-pin collisions must propagate (pins knock over other pins)
- Ball decelerates due to friction
- Gutter ball: ball leaving lane width cannot hit pins
- Pin count must match visible standing/toppled pins

Output a single HTML file.
physics_constraints: Impulse-based collision response for ball-pin and pin-pin. Ball curve from spin lateral force F_hook = 0.3 * omega_y * v_z. Pin toppling with gravity torque above 15-degree tilt. Lane friction 0.5 m/s^2 deceleration. Restitution 0.3 (ball-pin), 0.4 (pin-pin). Pin cascade through multi-body collision. Ball mass 6kg, pin mass 1.5kg.
difficulty_analysis: L5: (1) Impulse-based collision response with mass ratios for ball-pin and pin-pin; (2) Pin toppling dynamics with gravity torque; (3) Ball hook/curve physics from spin; (4) O(n^2) pin-pin collision detection and cascade; (5) Pin standing/toppled classification from tilt angle; (6) Game state machine (aim/rolling/scoring/reset); (7) Score tracking with strike detection; (8) Gutter detection and ball containment.
